title: Read before you build
intro: Words are parts too. These rules keep labels, messages and help text consistent across every screen, whether a person or an agent writes them. They follow the GOV.UK Design System, GitLab Pajamas and NN/g research.

rules.title: Write in sentence case
rules.text: Capitalize only the first word and proper nouns in labels, titles, buttons and badges. Title Case is harder to scan and reads as shouting in long labels.

rules.title: Buttons say what happens
rules.text: Start with a verb and name the thing it acts on. A person should know the result before they click.

rules.title: No vague labels
rules.text: "Submit", "Click here", "Yes" and "More" say nothing out of context. Screen reader users often hear a list of every link or button on the page, with no surrounding text.

rules.title: Errors say what went wrong and how to fix it
rules.text: Name the problem in plain words and tell the person what to do. Don't blame, don't use codes, don't say "invalid".

rules.title: Show errors at the right moment
rules.text: Check a field when the person leaves it or submits the form, not while they type its first value. Once a field shows an error, clear it as soon as the value is fixed. After a failed submit, list every error at the top of the form, each linked to its field.
rules.do: There is a problem: Enter your email address
rules.dont: Email is invalid (shown after the first keystroke)

rules.title: Mark optional fields, not required ones
rules.text: Ask only for what you need, then add "(optional)" to the few fields people may skip. Rows of asterisks add noise and need a legend.

rules.title: Keep punctuation light
rules.text: No full stops on buttons, titles, labels or badges. Use full stops in help text and messages that are sentences. Avoid exclamation marks.

rules.title: Write numbers and dates the same way everywhere
rules.text: Use numerals for numbers, the full month name in dates and a consistent time format. Avoid ambiguous dates like 03/04.

rules.title: Write for everyone
rules.text: Use plain words, active voice and "you". Avoid idioms, jargon and gendered defaults. Describe what something does, not how it looks ("select", not "click the blue button").
rules.dont: Just hit the big blue button, guys
